I am an old woman now, 71 years, and this small plot of fruit trees near my home is what I care for with my own hands. I cannot afford the chemical fertilizer from the market — the price has gone too high for a widow like me — but I collect manure from my few animals and spread it around the trees, as my husband taught me long ago. The trees are old ones I planted years back, so I do not buy new seed, and I have no money for sprays or pumps; I carry water only in the dry weeks when a tree looks weak. My grandson helps me sometimes on weekends, but most of the work is just me, slowly, through the season.
